questions.q: In the Brightleaf Outfitters case study, what initially tipped finance off that something was wrong?
options: The revenue report's number didn't match the POS system's own daily totals added up by hand
The report's dashboard tile displayed an error message
An auditor found a missing invoice
The POS system crashed during business hours
questions.explain: The report showed $2.1M while the POS system's own totals came to roughly $2.3M, a discrepancy finance noticed by comparing the two.

questions.q: What was the actual root cause the analyst found when tracing the lineage at the column level?
options: A filter condition meant to exclude voided transactions was also excluding legitimate after-hours sales, due to a POS-side labeling change
The warehouse table ran out of storage space
The dashboard was reading from the wrong year's data entirely
A currency conversion rate was outdated
questions.explain: A recent change to how the POS system tagged transactions caused legitimate late sales to be excluded by a filter that was only supposed to remove voided transactions.

questions.q: Why would a table-level lineage arrow (stg.Transactions_Clean to dw.FactSales) not have been enough to find this bug?
options: Because the bug was in a specific column-level filter condition, which a table-level arrow doesn't show
Because table-level lineage arrows are always drawn incorrectly
Because the bug had nothing to do with any transformation step
Because dw.FactSales does not actually exist in this scenario
questions.explain: The problem lived inside the specific filter logic of one transformation step — visible only at column-level lineage, not at the coarser table-level view.

questions.q: What did the impact-analysis step reveal before the fix was made?
options: Three other reports also depended on the same broken transformation step, so the bug had quietly affected more than just revenue
No other systems depended on the broken step at all
The bug only affected a single customer's account
The POS system itself needed to be completely replaced
questions.explain: Checking what else read from stg.Transactions_Clean and dw.FactSales.NetRevenue showed the bug had been silently affecting revenue, inventory depletion, and commission calculations.

questions.q: Besides fixing the filter logic, what else did the case study's fix include?
options: Updating the lineage record itself to precisely document the filter condition and flag the fragile dependency on the POS field
Deleting the lineage record since it was no longer needed
Switching the company to a completely different reporting tool
Removing column-level lineage from the pipeline going forward
questions.explain: The fix wasn't just a code change — the lineage documentation was updated to reflect reality and flag the fragile dependency on a field whose meaning had already changed once.
